script:
[HOOK]
If you've got an Apple Silicon Mac and you want to generate AI images without paying for cloud services, this is the exact setup I use on my 64GB Mac Studio. I'll show you how to run Stable Diffusion locally, completely free, and the tool I recommend makes it dead simple.

[INTRO]
Running Stable Diffusion locally on a Mac used to be a pain. You had to mess with Python environments, command line tools, and model downloads. But now there's an app that handles all of that for you. I've been running SDXL on my Mac Studio for a while, and it's become part of my daily creative workflow. Local generation means no subscription fees, no image limits, and your prompts stay on your machine. That's a big deal if you care about privacy or just want to experiment without watching a credit counter.

[BODY]
The tool I use is called DiffusionBee. It's a free, open-source app designed specifically for Apple Silicon Macs. It bundles Stable Diffusion models, including SDXL, into a simple interface. Here's how to get started.

First, download DiffusionBee from the link in the description. It's a standard Mac app, so just drag it to your Applications folder. Open it, and on first launch it will download the default model. That might take a few minutes depending on your internet. Once that's done, you're ready to generate.

The interface is straightforward. You type a prompt, hit generate, and it creates an image. For example, if I type "a cozy cabin in the woods at sunset, golden light, photorealistic", it will generate that in a few seconds on my Mac Studio. On a base M1 Mac it might take a bit longer, but it's still usable.

DiffusionBee also lets you load other models. If you want to use SDXL, you can download it from within the app. I've run SDXL locally on my 64GB Mac Studio and it works well, though it uses more memory. For most people, the default model is fine, but SDXL gives you better quality for complex scenes.

One thing I like is that it has built-in options like negative prompts, image-to-image, and inpainting. So you can refine your results without leaving the app. And because everything runs locally, you can generate as many images as you want, even offline.

[CTA]
So if you want to run Stable Diffusion on your Mac without the hassle, give DiffusionBee a try. It's free, and the download link is in the description. I've been using it for my own projects, and it's the fastest way I've found to get local AI image generation on Apple Silicon. If you found this helpful, a like and subscribe really helps the channel. Thanks for watching.
